summary: The rewrite of trimLiterals as an iterative indexOf walk faithfully reproduces the old regex's behavior while eliminating the stack overflow on ~15M-character literals (old code confirmed to throw RangeError on that size; new code trims it in ~20ms). Equivalence was verified by fuzzing ~480k inputs (exhaustive up to length 7 over quotes/double quotes/spaces/tabs/newlines, plus random and multi-megabyte cases) with zero mismatches, including the subtle unclosed-literal backtracking and post-match rescan semantics. All acceptance criteria are covered by passing tests and worst-case inputs (15M spaces, 7.5M escaped-quote pairs, 100k literals) complete in linear time.

findings.claim: The variable `const len = sql.length;` is declared but never used anywhere in the function (the walk uses sql.indexOf/sql.slice directly). Dead code left over from the rewrite.
findings.repro: grep -n '\blen\b' tools/sql-literals.mjs  # only the declaration on line 43 and an unrelated comment on line 3
